narrative:
**Week of 2026-08-17 — Hugging Face developer activity**

The most notable feature of this week's snapshot was Qwen's dominance of the classified model base: 8,397 of 24,465 tracked models (34.3%) resolved to the Qwen family, ahead of the generic "other-open" bucket at 4,484 (18.3%) and Llama at 1,189 (4.9%). Every other family sat in the low single digits — Gemma 657 (2.7%), Mistral 111, DeepSeek 107, NVIDIA Nemotron 103, GLM/Zhipu 58, Kimi/Moonshot 32. An important caveat: 9,327 models (38.1%) remained family-unknown, so the family mix is derived from roughly 62% of the corpus and Qwen's true share could shift materially as classification coverage improves. Engagement across the same 24,465 models totaled 9,237,513 downloads (≈378 per model) and 10,073 likes; the 5,842 tracked Spaces drew 739 likes. This delivery contained no prior-period values (1-week, 4-week and 12-week deltas were all null), so no week-over-week movement can be reported — the figures below are levels, not trends.

On the Spaces side, static builds led the SDK mix at 3,088 of 5,842 (52.9%), followed by Gradio at 2,049 (35.1%), Docker at 531 (9.1%) and Streamlit at 108 (1.8%), with 66 (1.1%) unclassified. By use case, "other" absorbed 1,822 Spaces (31.2%), a large residual bucket that limits interpretation; among named categories, chat-assistant led with 903 (15.5%), then image-generation 582 (10.0%), data-analysis 461 (7.9%), document-AI 341 (5.8%), voice-audio 339 (5.8%), search-research 337 (5.8%) and video-generation 315 (5.4%). Robotics (41 Spaces), music-generation (55) and 3D/gaming (110) remained niche. Within coding Spaces (111 family-tagged), Qwen (35.1%, 39) and other-open (34.2%, 38) were effectively tied, with Llama third at 9.9% (11); in chat-assistant (474 tagged), other-open led at 38.8% (184), Qwen followed at 32.1% (152), and proprietary APIs accounted for 12.0% (57). Family splits for 3D/gaming (24), music-generation (29), "other" (36), education (20) and robotics (20) rest on denominators below the reporting threshold in several sub-buckets and are too few to report as percentages.

Technology tagging showed vision-language at 6.97% of Spaces (407), agentic at 6.47% (378), diffusion at 5.36% (313) and multimodal at 5.31% (310), while frontier-adjacent tags stayed thin: MoE 0.62% (36) and long-context 0.33% (19). Vertical penetration was led by media-entertainment 9.72% (568) and consumer 9.40% (549), with education 7.34% (429) and scientific-research 7.12% (416) close behind; legal (0.89%, 52) and cybersecurity (1.85%, 108) trailed. Next week, the key thing to watch is whether comparison periods populate so we can measure movement — particularly whether Qwen's share holds as the 38.1% unknown-family segment gets classified.
